articles.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
articles.summary: An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose.
body: Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.”

Bournemouth’s new head coach has described the chaos of English football, midfield areas that can resemble a rolling maul, but he has pledged to learn and adapt. “I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation,” Rose said. “If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it’s hard to beat us. That’s what we should take into the next game.”

articles.summary: Sage loses 3-2 to former side; Benfica 4-1 Celtic. Juventus go top with 2-1 win over Celta Vigo. Pierre Sage endured a frustrating return to Lyon in the Europa League as his Crystal Palace side lost 3-2 to his former employers at the Groupama Stadium.
body: Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half without a shot on target for the visitors. Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the Ligue 1 side’s two-goal advantage. The Palace substitute Daichi Kamada pulled one back with nine minutes remaining in a better second half for Palace, who could not find an equaliser.

Days after beating his predecessor, the Nottingham Forest manager, Oliver Glasner, at Selhurst Park in the Premier League on Sunday, Sage found himself returning to the home of the club he managed for 14 months.
Ismaïla Sarr, who claimed the Conference League golden boot last season, was in the Crystal Palace starting lineup for the first time this season.

The Colombia striker Jhon Durán scored for the hosts with a penalty after just five minutes having been fouled by Dane Murray and completed his double in the 35th minute, after the defender Alexander Bah had doubled Benfica’s lead earlier in the half.

articles.title: Noah Sadiki stunner earns Sunderland dramatic late win against Torreense
articles.summary: Three minutes into stoppage time Noah Sadiki hurdled a set of advertising hoardings, sprinted across a running track and hurled himself towards the ecstatic Sunderland fans.
body: Just as those supporters’ long-awaited party in Portugal had looked in peril of falling a little flat, the Democratic Republic of the Congo midfielder capitalised on excellent work from Enzo Le Fée and Granit Xhaka to half-volley an eye-catching first goal for Régis Le Bris’s side.

It ensured a largely unconvincing Sunderland came from behind to secure a second straight Europa League win and their relief was evident as every outfield player followed Sadiki in vaulting those hoardings to join the celebrations.
“It was a difficult game,” said Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager, with considerable understatement. “Torreense are a good team.”

With their home ground too small to accommodate European football, Leiria’s stadium stood in. It proved quite some substitute. An arena overlooked by a 12th-century castle constructed to defend this attractive medieval town against reconquest by the Moors created an imposing backdrop to Sunderland’s first competitive trip to the continent for 53 years.

articles.summary: De La Salle-Concord's juggernaut football team will be in the spotlight as it faces unbeaten Monte Vista on Friday in Danville. Here's more on that matchup and other top games.
body: De La Salle-Concord's juggernaut football team will defeat unbeaten Monte Vista 46-7 Friday in Danville - at least, that's the outcome projected by the long-running model at HSRatings.com.

He and the Mustangs simply remain focused on their preparations, as they've done during a 7-0 start and coming off a surprising North Coast Section Division 2 title, their first since 2016, ninth overall and fourth since Wingert won one as a senior guard in 2001.

As impressive as Monte Vista's resurgence has been, ending De La Salle's 285-game unbeaten streak (the last loss was in 1991) against NCS opponents is a tall order. The last time the Mustangs beat De La Salle was 14-13 for the 1987 NCS 3A title at the Oakland Coliseum in one of the more famous championship title tilts in section history. That broke a De La Salle 44-game win streak.

"We're not going to reinvent the wheel, that's for sure," Wingert said of preparing for De La Salle. "We're putting in maybe one new play and a few different formations. We don't have the biggest or most athletic kids, but we're not preparing to play NFL players - not yet, anyway. They're just high school kids, albeit very good and hard working ones."

articles.title: ‘There are no words': Dan Orlovsky asks for help after brother-in-law's death
articles.summary: Dan Orlovsky, an ESPN football analyst and Connecticut native, turned to the public for support after his brother-in-law died unexpectedly over the weekend. In a post on X, Orlovsky, who played as a quarterback for the University of Connecticut, said the death of his sister Christine's husband…
body: "There are no words to describe the heartbreak of losing a husband, a partner, and a father so suddenly," he said. "In the midst of trying to process this devastating loss, my sister is now facing the overwhelming reality of navigating life as a solo parent and a single-income household, all while helping her boys cope with the loss of their dad."
Orlovsky shared a GoFundMe fundraiser set up for his sister's family, which had raised $107,000 of its $150,000 goal as of Thursday at 5:30 p.m.

"No family should have to face this kind of heartbreak, and no one should have to worry about how they will manage financially while trying to put the pieces of their lives back together," he said. "We are asking for your help in supporting my sister and her boys during this incredibly painful and uncertain time. Any donation, no matter the amount, will help ease some of the financial burden and allow them the time and space they need to grieve, heal, and begin navigating this new reality."

articles.title: ESPN’s PTI, hosted by Michael Wilbon and Tony Kornheiser, celebrates 25th anniversary on October 22
articles.summary: One of ESPN’s most successful programs, Pardon the Interruption, also known as PTI, is celebrating its 25th anniversary on October 22, 2026. Hosted by Michael Wilbon and Tony Kornheiser, the program has been a mainstay at ESPN since its inception.
body: Wilbon and Kornheiser use graphics and a timer to stay on task as they tackle the top sports topics of the day. They will host back-to-back 30 minute episodes on October 22 beginning at 5 PM EDT.

Wilbon and Kornheiser were longtime Washington Post reporters who went on the air weeks after the 9/11 tragedy. The show got its start in an era when cell phones and social media were not integral to the sports world.
They have managed to keep the show fresh despite a dramatic change in the way fans watch and absorb sports news over the past 25 years.

What has not changed is the duo is surrounded by an ecletic assortment of sports and entertainment memorabilia, bobbleheads, and novelty items. The two also shout out to the Canadian fans at the conclusion of each episode.

articles.title: Al Michaels gets candid on retirement before Broncos-Seahawks game
articles.summary: On Thursday night the Denver Broncos square off against the Seattle Seahawks in a battle of playoff team hoping to pick up their fourth win of the season. On the call for Thursday night’s game is legendary play-by-play man Al Michaels, who turns 82 years old next month.
body: However, it doesn’t seem like Michaels is ready to hand the microphone over just yet. Dan Patrick asked Michaels in a new interview when he knows it’ll be time to hang up the mic – but he’s not going away easily.
In response to being asked how he’ll find out it’s time to retire Michaels said, “Well, either the people that I work for will tell me, or I’ll know myself, a combination.”

“Let’s put it this way. The folks at Amazon and Prime have been fantastic. Fantastic to me,” he said before revealing Amazon checks in with him after every season to gauge his interest in returning to the booth.
As of right now it seems like Michaels is comfortable riding out his current contract before making a final decision on the broadcasting future.

articles.title: Rutter scores twice as Brighton win big and go top in Conference League
articles.summary: Georginio Rutter scored twice and set up one as Brighton thrashed Kauno Zalgris 4-0 to get their Conference League campaign off to a winning start.
body: Brighton were dominant from the first whistle to the last against the Lithuanian Cup winners and took the lead through Rutter, but only after a VAR check. The ball had initially been deemed to have gone out of play before Ibrahim Osman's cut-back to the Frenchman, but the goal was awarded after review.

Rutter then turned provider as Brighton doubled their lead on the stroke of half-time when Hinshelwood - returning to the side for the first time since the Premier League opening weekend - slotted into the corner.
The third came after a lung-bursting run from Malick Yalcouye, who played Osman through to cross for Rutter to turn into the net with ease.

Matt O'Riley made it four with a header as he scored his first Brighton goal since August 2025. The Australia international should have got his second with another header late on, but was denied by an excellent save from Tomas Svedkauskas.

body: The breakaway league is attempting to relaunch next year with new money from BC Partners Capital after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support having ploughed in $5bn (£3.7bn) over four years.
But in order to do that it has had to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and, as a result, it has had to cancel the contracts of the existing players so they can be re-signed on new terms to LIV 2.0.

However, the DP World Tour confirmed this week it was taking a harder line than previously and any player committing to LIV 2.0 would be ineligible for its membership and therefore also ruled out of Ryder Cup contention.

It has been seen in many quarters as an attempt to deliver the final blow to LIV's fading hopes of survival and, according to reports in the US media, its attorney Robert Fitzgerald told the US Bankruptcy Court in New York: "We're continuing to monitor this situation very closely and we're quite concerned by it frankly.
